Two randomized human controlled trials report reduced acute procedural pain with topical clove preparations: a split-mouth placebo-controlled trial in 73 adults found glycerin gel prepared with ground clove lowered dental needle-insertion pain versus placebo (PMID16530911, p=.005), and a double-blind crossover in 34 hemodialysis patients found topical eugenol nanoemulsion lowered cannulation puncture pain versus no intervention and placebo gel (PMID32951708, p=.001; placebo mean omitted from public abstract). Competing studies show inconclusive three-arm postoperative headache contrasts for inhaled clove aromatherapy (PMID40012817, p=.20 at 8 h and p=.31 at 24 h), an unquantified null mouse hot-water report for ground clove powder (CCRAS 1997-1998), and assay-dependent rat essential-oil nanogel formalin versus hot-plate results (PMC9123718). Topical procedural versus oral chronic Parkinson pain and competing null trials keep the easing signal at minimal_signal.

One controlled mouse experiment (Bian 2019; 10 mice per group across five arms) reports lower 20-minute acetic-acid-evoked writhing counts after oral volatile fractions from dry-fried (toasted) and raw huajiao versus vehicle (18.40 and 21.10 dry-fried, 19.50 and 27.20 raw vs 49.60 vehicle), although full-text methods, fried-versus-raw comparison, and botanical species voucher remain unverified. Local application of isolated hydroxy-alpha-sanshool reduced inflammatory mechanical hypersensitivity without altering heat hypersensitivity in mice (PMID23652591), an uncontrolled nine-woman xerostomia series of mixed Zanthoxylum oil capsules noted oral-discomfort gains without placebo (PMC6392883), and a 40-woman placebo-controlled IBS trial of multi-herb daikenchuto was null for abdominal and rectal pain without isolating Sichuan pepper (PMID26486374). Volatile-fraction rather than whole toasted spice, unverified full-text details, multi-herb clinical nullity, and absence of Parkinson pain data keep the easing signal at minimal_signal.

One double-blind randomized placebo-controlled trial in 82 healthy adults aged 30-55 (Kennedy 2019, PMID31835620, PMC6950039, NCT03673930) reports lower day-56 cognitive-task mental fatigue with 80 mg/day standardized Zanthoxylum armatum extract in MCT oil versus sunflower-oil placebo (p=.006), although pretreatment mental fatigue was already higher in the extract arm and primary registered endpoint was chronic secondary memory. Two healthy-gamer extract crossover registrations with fatigue outcomes (NCT07047105, NCT07752329) have no posted results. Standardized extract versus culinary ground Sichuan pepper, non-Parkinson healthy sample, and baseline imbalance keep the easing signal at minimal_signal.

One randomized four-arm trial in 104 adults with functional dyspepsia (85 analyzed; Saravani 2025, PMID40365186, PMC12068504) reports greater week-8 constipation subscore improvement for aqueous Rhus coriaria (sumac) extract alone (n=24) and combined with eating-habit changes (n=25) versus omeprazole (n=25) in adjusted model 6 (p=.002 and p<.001) with zero adverse events, although unadjusted contrasts were unstated and effect magnitudes/confidence intervals were omitted from Table 6. Conversely, a preclinical mouse castor-oil diarrhea and rabbit jejunum study found crude sumac extract slowed induced diarrhea and relaxed intestinal contractions (DOI10.3329/bjp.v9i4.20879). Active omeprazole comparator, aqueous extract versus ground sumac, non-Parkinson dyspepsia cohort, and unreported effect sizes keep the easing lean contradicting the worsening hypothesis at minimal_signal.

One published human clinical case of focal eyelid dystonia (blepharospasm; Leon-Sarmiento 2005, PMID16258648) reports a decline in rated dystonia severity from 4 at baseline to 1 at six months following transdermal capsaicin patch treatment, alongside an inconclusive blink-rate check in five healthy volunteers (17 +- 3 vs 15 +- 5). Uncontrolled single-patient design, topical isolated capsaicin patch rather than oral ground cayenne pepper, and focal non-Parkinson blepharospasm rather than Parkinson dystonia keep the easing signal at minimal_signal.

One double-blind randomized placebo-controlled crossover in healthy volunteers (Tanaka 2008; 18 randomized, 17 analyzed) reports smaller visual-analogue fatigue increases after 29 days of oral chicken-breast extract drink (400 mg/day imidazole dipeptides) versus placebo following four hours of cycling (+18.1 +- 15.8 vs +26.3 +- 18.1 mm, p<.05) and four hours of recovery (+9.8 +- 17.3 vs +20.1 +- 20.7 mm, p<.01), whereas two-hour, next-day, and end-of-exercise recovery contrasts were null; food chemistry confirms anserine and carnosine retention in heated chicken breast (DOI10.3136/nskkk.66.210). Conversely, a 30-adult randomized crossover of reconstituted whole-chicken soup found inconclusive routine POMS fatigue changes (-0.5 vs +0.1, p=.61; DOI10.1248/jhs.55.56), a sprint extract trial had inconclusive power outcomes (PMID16531904), and a culinary patent tasting report (KR20050019309A) lacks controlled symptom measurement. Concentrated dipeptide drink versus poached chicken, healthy exercise-induced fatigue rather than Parkinson fatigue, small sample, and competing null chicken-soup crossover keep the easing signal at minimal_signal.

Oral isolated curcumin improved mean open-field speed or timed pole descent in independent Parkinson-model rodent comparisons. The original Ramkumar study used an isolated derivative and balance-dependent beam, rotarod and hanging tasks, so its broader motor outcomes contribute context. A human registry outside Parkinson disease reported 0.089 m/s less walking-speed gain with curcumin than placebo in 17 older adults, with no posted between-arm analysis. The adverse skilled-reaching result concerns task success in young mice. Ghodsi's nanomicelle trial and Donadio's phospholipid cohort supply composite Parkinson motor scores without a separate bradykinesia estimate. The close animal timing outcomes retain a minimal easing signal despite conflicting indirect human walking evidence and the unresolved culinary exposure.

Two independent randomized placebo-controlled human trials of coated proprietary Cucumis melo cantaloupe juice concentrate (Extramel 10 mg/day) report reduced subjective fatigue in stressed or healthy adults: a four-week trial in 70 adults reported 26% greater day-28 FARD weariness improvement versus placebo (Milesi 2009, PMID19754931, PMC2757026), and an 84-day trial in 61 healthy adults reported lower day-84 Prevost physical fatigue versus placebo (84.4 vs 93.2, p<.02; day-28 null; Carillon 2014, PMID24949549, PMC4073155, NCT01767922). Conversely, three competing randomized trials of melon SOD/gliadin or dried melon concentrate were null on fatigue (Houghton 2010 PMID21044831 n=38; SODB 2020 PMID32053942 p=.068; GliSODin 2022 PMID35628874 n=46 p=.15). Proprietary palm-oil-coated concentrate versus raw cantaloupe, non-Parkinson cohorts, and three competing null trials keep the easing lean at minimal_signal.

One double-blind randomized placebo-controlled trial in 82 healthy adults aged 30-55 (Kennedy 2019, PMID31835620, PMC6950039, NCT03673930) reports faster acute Speed of Attention (p=.039) and fewer rapid visual information processing false alarms (p=.025) with 80 mg/day standardized Zanthoxylum armatum extract in MCT oil versus sunflower-oil placebo, while baseline false alarms were higher in the extract arm, name-to-face memory accuracy moved unfavorably (p=.040), and chronic secondary memory was the registered primary endpoint. Two healthy-gamer extract crossover registrations targeting attention speed and accuracy (NCT07047105, NCT07752329) have no posted results. Standardized extract versus culinary toasted Sichuan pepper, healthy non-Parkinson sample, mixed cognitive domain signs, and baseline imbalance keep the easing lean contradicting the worsening hypothesis at minimal_signal.

Multiple independent controlled Parkinson-model rodent experiments report improved locomotor speed, open-field movement, or reduced drug-induced catalepsy and extrapyramidal movement signs with Nigella sativa seed extracts, seed oil, or thymoquinone: oral isolated thymoquinone increased rotenone-mouse open-field distance and movement speed (PMID40951472, n=3/arm; beam/wire inconclusive), isolated thymoquinone improved chlorpromazine-rat catalepsy and locomotion (PMID27180446), oral Nigella sativa oil 0.2 mL/rat reduced haloperidol-induced EPS movement disorders and oral dyskinesia (Malik 2016, PMID27752803; abstract-level depth), oral Nigella oil increased open-field activity in rotenone rats (DOI10.21608/ejh.2024.304554.2104; design discrepancies noted), and higher Nigella seed extract doses lowered drug-induced mouse catalepsy (DOI10.4236/wjns.2014.44035). Conversely, a single-plant hydroalcoholic Nigella seed extract haloperidol catalepsy experiment was inconclusive (PMID41438691). Animal-only models, oil/extract/constituent exposures rather than culinary ground nigella seed, small group sizes, and the competing null catalepsy study keep the easing signal contradicting the worsening hypothesis at minimal_signal.

Two independent controlled studies converge in an easing direction for oral pumpkin seed oil on depressive symptoms: a 12-week double-blind randomized human trial in 35 postmenopausal women (31 analyzed; Gossell-Williams 2011, PMID21545273) reported median depression item staying at 0 (IQR 0-1) on 2 g/day Cucurbita pepo seed oil versus rising from 0 to 1 (IQR 0-2) on wheat germ oil (unadjusted endpoint p=.046 across 18 exploratory items), and a six-week chronic mild stress rat experiment (DOI10.21608/ejchem.2024.310875.10173, grouped with the related 2022 cortical report as one program) reported higher sucrose preference and shorter tail-suspension immobility with oral pumpkin seed oil versus stressed controls. Active wheat-germ-oil comparator, floor effect, unverified cold-press extraction, exploratory single-item rating, and absence of a Parkinson cohort keep the easing lean at minimal_signal.

Three independent controlled rodent sleep experiments using Perilla frutescens (shiso) leaf preparations converge on an easing direction for sleep onset and duration: oral ethanolic Perillae Herba extract shortened pentobarbital-induced sleep latency in mice and increased total sleep in rats (Kwon 2017, DOI10.20307/nps.2017.23.1.53), oral Bacillus-fermented perilla leaf extract increased rodent NREM and slow-wave sleep and shortened sleep latency (Bormate 2024, DOI10.1016/j.jff.2024.106345), and inhaled perilla leaf essential oil shortened sleep latency and prolonged sleep duration in PCPA-induced insomnia mice alongside documented Traditional Chinese Medicine insomnia context (Zhong 2021, PMID33246117). Conversely, a randomized human functional-dyspepsia trial of an eight-herb perilla formula (NCT05948215, Liu 2024, PMID39256061; n=26) showed inconclusive within-arm PSQI changes (p=.207 vs p=.141) without isolating perilla, a Korean multi-herb depression trial lacked a separate insomnia estimate (SAR2025-113), and two combination registrations (KCT0012330, NCT05668104) have no posted results. Preclinical-only isolated leaf extracts/oil, absence of oral culinary dried shiso human trials, and non-Parkinson models keep the easing lean at minimal_signal.

Raw celery leaves contain butylphthalide, and human feeding studies show plasma apigenin. The pharmaceutical mouse report uses locomotion and coordination measures. A clinical butylphthalide registration planned Part IV motor complications and the likely matching conference report gives cognitive outcomes. Fresh celery leaf and clinical dyskinesia severity remain unresolved.

Primary PARK2 donor fibroblast assays did not administer sumac to the patients or measure facial expression.

A Parkinson diet trial had a canola-containing low-fat menu and an inconclusive Part IV motor-complications comparison. The claim needs separately reported daily off time after cold-pressed canola exposure.

Dried leaf extract gave similar stool-day and constipation-score changes to placebo. Seed-oil data favor a selected score in athletes. The mixed-tablet patent evidence differs by formulation and one table contradicts its narrative. No result isolates whole fresh shiso for constipation in Parkinson disease. The direction remains unresolved.
Exploratory movement after ground whole hazelnuts in high-fat-fed mice lacks the toasted oil, Parkinson population and freezing frequency endpoint.
Macadamia kernel poisoning causes weakness and impaired movement in dogs. The oil, disease population and bradykinesia measure remain untested.

The safflower comparator in a PSP registration is oral and explicitly named. The protocol gives a motor composite and no separate walking-speed result. Existing exercise and ataxia walking trajectories differ. The claim remains open for cold-pressed oil in Parkinson disease.
A Parkinson diet plan used tarragon in two recipes. It does not specify dried state or report individual consumption. MDS-UPDRS III totals do not give a facial-expression item effect.

A mixed-oil patent gives a patient impression of swallowing the product. The texture-modified food study assesses healthy-volunteer chewing and bolus properties. These exposures leave cold-pressed canola effects on Parkinson swallowing unresolved.
A placebo-controlled sage-tip extract trial found no clear difference in dream recall. The report gives no dream enactment count or ground-sage Parkinson comparison.

The Parkinson diet menu lists walnut oil without grade, individual assignment or a rigidity-item result. Cold-pressed walnut oil improved climbing in a fly toxin model, which does not measure rigidity. The two records leave the clinical direction open.

Green cardamom powder has isolated digestive adverse-event reports outside Parkinson disease. An uncontrolled cardamom-containing mixture improved composite IBS severity. Another mixture trial prints selected bowel comments and supplies no arm prevalence or validated constipation severity. The direction for ground cardamom remains open.

Anise seed extract and fraction studies use animal memory and exploratory tasks with differing results and formulations. No clinical executive impairment result after ground seed in Parkinson disease was established.

Injected DHA lengthened strides in lesioned rats. In older adults without Parkinson disease, fish oil plus training versus olive oil plus training gave time-by-group p = .753 for single-task stride and .537 for dual-task stride. The roles of oral whole trout and grilling remain unresolved.

Concentrated tarragon essential oil impaired motor performance or produced ataxia in injected animal toxicity and seizure-model studies. An oral extract study measured general maze activity. These exposures and endpoints leave the direction of fresh tarragon on Parkinson postural instability unresolved.
Open-field activity did not change significantly in mice given injected extract. The fruit-drink trial measured exercise pain and did not time Parkinson walking.
The menu analysis reports total UPDRS III without an isolated dried lovage exposure or dyskinesia-severity change.

Boiled sweet potato with stew was tested in a run-based oxygen uptake study. A separate steamed sweet potato rice cake trial measured immediate cycling exertion and found no clear difference. Neither study measured fatigue severity in Parkinson disease.

A small wristband patent reports improvement with topical grapeseed oil, and a Parkinson rat study measured stride and grid descent after hydroalcoholic seed extract. Registered oral oil work concerns grip strength and has no posted result.

Different curry leaf extracts improved toxin-model movement initiation or worsened a drug-model catalepsy proxy. The 2012 extract result at 120 minutes was 110.0 seconds, and the 2025 administration route remains unverified. The diet pilot does not isolate ground curry leaf or report clinical bradykinesia by food.
Basil odor was misidentified by 74.3% in a Parkinson diagnostic study. The stimulus was smelled during an identification test and the study gives no olfactory change after eating basil.

The memory-care poster model gives a lower combined NPI score with topical and diffused almond oil than with lavender. It reports no visual hallucination counts. Oral cold-pressed almond oil and Parkinson hallucination frequency remain unresolved.

In 97 people with Parkinson disease, gaining recognition of the coconut test odor was associated with worse standing lightheadedness scores (B = 1.147, nominal p = .003). The study used odor strips. The effect of consuming refined coconut oil remains unresolved.
A leaf-extract Parkinson model measured neuron histology and a separate leaf-oil seizure study reported motor impairment. Neither comparison measured stride length after culinary intake.

Parkinson depression trials used mineral or corn oil comparators. The blood fatty-acid preprint measures circulating levels and cannot identify intake. Outside Parkinson, varied sunflower comparators lack an oil-free arm, and two newly indexed registrations have no posted mood results. The refined-oil weight-loss trial still lacks accessible arm-level depression data. Evidence leaves the effect of isolated oral refined sunflower oil on Parkinson depressive symptoms unresolved.

Nutmeg solvent extracts changed spontaneous activity in healthy mice and some oral extract contrasts improved coordination in toxin or drug models. The higher dose in one solvent series was inconclusive. The studies leave ground nutmeg and clinical bradykinesia open.

Isolated oral capsaicin had divergent anxiety-like behavior findings in different rat models. A runner crossover shows an imprecise anxiety-event difference, and a human rocoto trial used another pepper species with insufficient group comparisons. Smoked paprika and clinical Parkinson anxiety remain untested.
Bay-leaf extracts and constituents affected gastric physiology in ethanol studies. No primary record measured levodopa exposure or daily OFF duration after ground leaf.
The low-fat trial menu includes baked apple crisp. The published Part IV total gives no item-level dystonia result or observed comparison by baked apple consumption.

Mouse pole performance improved after red pepper decoction and a Parkinson case reported better walking while receiving combination treatment. Neither study counted freezing episodes after eating toasted Sichuan pepper.
The Parkinson mint-gum study found no clear change in timed walking. Gum flavor and plant species are unresolved, and the trial did not test brewed spearmint.

In healthy students taking a cranberry drink, one depression-dejection subscale score was higher at week 4. Later values and the HADS depression comparisons were inconclusive. The separate mixed snack and extract studies leave the direction for dried cranberry and Parkinson depression open.

The apricot study tested a methanolic kernel extract and animal motor tests. A Parkinson crossover measured OFF time under a low-protein regimen and gives no raw apricot contrast. The frozen exposure remains unresolved.

Small Parkinson habanero-extract and isolated capsaicin trials measured acute timing with imprecise contrasts. The original Kyushu poster elicited swallows after brief local capsaicin contact in anesthetized rats. The independent Niigata line observed fewer mechanically triggered swallows after prolonged contact. A healthy-volunteer red-pepper sauce comparison favored brief preconditioning on a cued task, with no clear improvement under continuous exposure. The 2026 crossover administered the same capsaicinoids in both arms. These route, timing and outcome differences leave the effect of eating ground cayenne on clinical Parkinson swallowing difficulty open.

Corn-oil studies use a shared carrier, mixed or topical formulations, or tests outside Parkinson disease. Overnight polysomnography in healthy people gave inconclusive comparisons and used corn oil in both arms. Topical postherpetic neuralgia treatment measured global sleep quality. The adolescent protocol gives no verified sleep results. No rated Parkinson insomnia comparison isolates refined corn oil.

An egg-recipe trial found no clear effect on a physical performance composite that included an eight-foot walk. Two Parkinson studies list eggs among many foods. The recent observational abstract associates weekly egg intake with osteosarcopenia and gives gait results by diagnosis. An egg-specific walking estimate remains open.

The brewed spearmint osteoarthritis comparison did not separate pain by assigned tea. Other reports use mixed extracts, mint oils or a suspected topical allergy. Fresh oral spearmint and Parkinson pain remain unresolved.

People report using coconut oil among several strategies for coping with OFF periods. A separate qualitative high-fat meal account has no oil identification. The randomized medium-chain triglyceride comparison used an ordinal OFF result that differed before treatment. These do not give a refined coconut oil estimate for daily OFF time.

One commercial salt combines orange and saffron extracts and was evaluated for salty taste in people grouped by baseline smell function. It supplies no post-exposure olfactory impairment result in Parkinson disease.

Parkinson diet studies list peach without a participant-linked postural result. A prior-falls case provides medication management context, and a healthy-volunteer protocol uses peach juice in every arm. The studies give no raw peach and postural instability comparison.

An isolated rosemary compound and rosemary oil produced mixed motor proxy results across animals, with contradictory figure and text in one report. The human hypotension study judged blood pressure rather than clinical postural stability.

Bay-leaf tea reduced healthy adults' stress and anxiety. Higher-concentration rat decoction increased forced-swim immobility despite an abstract that describes decreased immobility overall. Neither measures apathy or identifies a ground bay-leaf direction in Parkinson disease.

A multicomponent rosemary spray improved pooled throat symptoms at 20 minutes with an inconclusive three-day result. The individual rosemary gargle and topical reports address postoperative hoarseness. Neither provides acoustic or clinically measured Parkinson voice volume after dried leaf consumption.
A prostate-disease study reported reduced urination frequency after an aqueous garlic extract without a control group. It did not count urgency episodes or assess cooked garlic in Parkinson’s.

A controlled ground-cinnamon crossover outside Parkinson disease had no clear daily stool-frequency contrast. Human cassia water-extract findings concern model-relevant transit during diarrhea. Extract experiments in constipated and diarrheal rats move pellet frequency in different directions under different conditions. The symptom-severity direction remains unresolved.

Human odor work measured ratings of other people's faces. Parkinson multiodor training includes eugenol but gives no facial expression subitem. The two inherited collections use clove terminology for an overgrowth acronym or imaging shape and add no ground clove hypomimia estimate.

Earlier injected dill preparations affected mouse movement and later oral extract work used a rodent coordination task. The mixed dill and rice stroke intervention gives broad activities and clinical totals. None tests manual dexterity after fresh dill weed in Parkinson disease.
Timed symbol counts increased on repeat testing in both the oral avocado comparator and CBD arms. The study does not isolate avocado oil or identify refining or manual dexterity impairment.

Parkinson diet-index comparisons reported associations with self-rated motivation. The pooled sofrito item and the mixed-food studies provide no verified braised-leek intake or separate apathy result.

Almond oil was a carrier patch in a Thai exercise trial reporting sway and fear of falls, and an almond-skin zebrafish experiment measured mobility. Neither counted Parkinson falls under oral cold-pressed oil exposure.
A patent describes a multiherb depression mixture containing powdered cardamom, then compares continued mixture with switching to placebo. It gives no Parkinson apathy estimate after ground cardamom.

The MPTP conference report describes akinesia and abnormal stepping, without a separate freezing event definition or count. The related thesis abstract gives no gait outcome result. Clinical freezing after ground paprika remains open.

A beverage study assessed sustained-vowel acoustics. An individual with corticobasal degeneration consumed milk in a late mixed diet after longstanding speech impairment. Dairy sensory trials and Parkinson incidence cohorts supply no pasteurized cow's milk and listener-intelligibility comparison.

Isolated myrcene changed barbiturate-induced sleep under injection, oral and inhaled conditions, with opposite associations across acute and repeated oral schedules. The leaf-food comparison in Parkinson insomnia remains open.

Garden lovage appears in a multicomponent Parkinson menu without a dream-enactment result. Prospective diet-pattern work measures probable REM behavior disorder before diagnosis and does not isolate dried lovage or count episodes.
Turkey aroma chemistry characterizes the food and pooled poultry intake produced an inconclusive total symptom estimate. Neither assesses smell impairment after baked turkey.

Rodent tarragon preparations increased selected exploration, grooming or social measures. Sucrose preference was inconclusive, and a reported social-test p value conflicts with the printed statistic. Extracts and behavioral proxies give no directional estimate for dried culinary tarragon and Parkinson apathy.

Concentrated fruit extract impaired rotarod retention in healthy mice. Two Parkinson-model reports found improved performance under different extraction and exposure regimens. No study measured postural instability after toasted seeds in people with Parkinson’s.

Both post-COVID groups received the same ungraded oral peanut oil and reported joint pain. Animal and topical comparisons use other routes. A dopamine nanoparticle experiment used peanut oil as a carrier and did not measure pain. Refined peanut oil and clinical Parkinson pain remain unresolved.

A cooked chervil soup allergy case describes acute airway and voice symptoms with no visual hallucinations. The Parkinson diet menu does not report hallucinations by herb. Poisoning cases involving other Apiaceae do not identify garden chervil.

The Parkinson whole-diet comparison aggregated motor complications and reported a ketogenic-arm dyskinesia case involving changes in medication. A separately measured severity effect from cold-pressed canola remains unresolved.
Estragole from another plant oil alters isolated skeletal-muscle contractile responses; it is not tarragon administration or patterned dystonia in a living Parkinson patient.

The Tartary buckwheat sprout-powder preprint found an inconclusive primary cognitive result and mixed exploratory performance, including faster Flanker and Stroop responses and less improvement on one sustained-attention variability measure. It did not test toasted groats or Parkinson’s.

Parkinson constipation handout lists chervil among fiber-containing herbs, but supplies no consumption comparison, preparation-specific exposure or patient bowel outcomes. Chervil-soup allergy case describes acute throat and voice changes, not constipation.

Healthy adults assigned soy-oil capsules reported nearly unchanged sleep-quality scores after eight weeks. The only drowsiness complaint was in the lysolecithin arm. The registry postdates follow-up and lists no separate sleepiness endpoint. Oil refining and a Parkinson daytime sleepiness effect remain unresolved.

A paprika oleoresin trial in adults with mild knee pain found no clear pain-VAS or total JKOM contrast. A separate carotenoid trial lists adverse events in both groups and did not measure pain severity. The registered knee study has no reported results and its match to the paper is unverified.
A Parkinson diet trial analyzed an everyday motor aggregate that includes handwriting without giving the handwriting item or size. Independent cold-pressed canola effects remain unresolved.
Oral eugenol shortened narrow-beam crossing when given before toxin exposure and prolonged crossing after exposure in mice. Clinical fall frequency after ground clove remains untested.

Oral comparator arms using peanut oil show some within-arm improvement in depression scores. These include healthy volunteers, irritable bowel syndrome and a vitamin D trial, all without an independent refined-oil comparison. The peanut-only arm of a topical and inhalational trial also improved. Planned diabetes program depression results are unavailable. These exposures and populations leave direction unresolved for refined peanut oil in Parkinson disease.

An individual case improved after powdered nutmeg in milk. The student infusion reports lack a usable between-group estimate or combine sleep education. A separate mace-aril study lacked a comparator, and the mixed-botanical trial was inconclusive across active arms. Parkinson insomnia remains open.

A Parkinson thesis used a multiingredient honey mixture containing anise seed. It reports no handwriting-size outcome tied to intake. Isolated anise oil and constituent studies used different motor measures.

UMIN000018516 reports no difference in hoarseness or itching after multiherb Hange-koboku-to versus no formula around intubation; no counts or loudness data and the tested brand or perilla content is not confirmed.

An older-adult trial of tulsi and cardamom extract did not publish a clear between-arm change in its accessible abstract. A Crohn trial measuring depression included cardamom in both groups. Ground cardamom and Parkinson depression remain unresolved.

Isolated beta-caryophyllene improved a mouse pole-task time, and eugenol had opposing movement patterns before and after MPTP. Injected essential oil studies add different animal motor proxies. The effects do not resolve the direction for culinary ground clove and clinical bradykinesia.

Black mustard seed extract improved general activity in drug-treated rats. The motor tests leave step and stride geometry unmeasured, while the toasted preparation and clinical Parkinson gait comparison remain open.
Oral avocado oil was associated with fewer rotations in a unilateral Huntington-like injury model. The publication family did not establish cold pressing or assess dystonic movements.

A ground sumac hypertension trial reported zero insomnia events versus one on placebo and an invalid printed p value. Historical sumac sleep use and unrelated seed-extract schedules add no comparative insomnia severity result. The sparse adverse-event data do not supply a direction.

The oral comparator gives no clear within-arm anxiety change and differs from roasted peanuts. Topical peanut carrier reports and a composite mouse oil substitution give no independent human oil contrast. The diabetes support trial reports only program-level anxiety. Cold-pressed peanut oil and clinical Parkinson anxiety remain unresolved.

The Parkinson cohort documents oregano use without an individual drooling result. Oral oil jelly measured pH, with drooling as the sample method. The effervescent dosage-form patent describes salivation without a clinical fresh-oregano comparison.

The dried-leaf infusion pilot reports Parkinson nonmotor totals with no separate attention estimate. Nasal oil studies measured EEG or stress and the mouse study measured memory after injected extract. None measured attention impairment after eating fresh marjoram.

A Parkinson diet pilot listed pumpkin seed oil and included rigidity in a composite score without giving separate effects. In one rotenone mouse experiment, seed extract shortened bar-test immobility late and prolonged it at a lower dose earlier. Toasted oil and clinical rigidity remain open.
Parkinson inpatient mixed vegetarian menu listed parsley; UPDRS III total improved but individual herb intake, drying and stride-length changes were not reported.

The original allspice oil abstract reports oral irritation and sedation in rats. A related speech-loss case involved a different clove oil and alcohol. Neither measures human speech intelligibility or clinical change after ground allspice.

The oral clove study's anxiety-labelled table corresponds to Beck depression methods and has no separate anxiety test. A Parkinson multi-odor trial reports anxiety changes but did not isolate eugenol or ground clove. The frozen direction remains unresolved.

Oral common chive leaf extract in stroke-model mice had neurological and Morris water-maze outcomes; abstract contains no anxiety result. Ferulic acid studies are isolated constituent rather than dried chives.
A model tested isolated lentinan and surveillance recorded skin reactions to raw or undercooked shiitake. Neither assessed clinical postural instability after cooked shiitake.
Parsley appeared in a mixed Parkinson diet menu; no assigned fresh-leaf exposure or separate hand dexterity or finger-tapping item results appear.

The marjoram tea pilot measured composite nonmotor and depression scores. The Tlemcen mixture thesis lists sleep disturbance across the survey. Separate insomnia severity after consuming dried marjoram remains unresolved. Related cultural/experiential records (1) provide uncontrolled context without changing the open efficacy rating.

A fetal study and its neonatal follow-up examined facial behavior around kale flavor exposure. Roasted kale laboratory work measured aroma and a sensory rehabilitation study listed kale as optional. None isolates eating roasted kale against clinical olfactory impairment in Parkinson disease.

A Parkinson whole-diet comparison used boiled potato in mixed meals and did not isolate its effect on sleepiness. A pediatric mash crossover registered acute sleepiness and the probable linked abstract omits that outcome. Frying and baking protocols measure related symptoms with no boiled-potato result.

A Parkinson diagnostic test used dried sage as an odor. A separate common-sage oil aromatherapy study required intact smell and measured satisfaction. The effect of consuming ground sage on clinical olfaction remains unknown.

Both Parkinson diet menus permit kale or spinach and individual choices are unverified. The urinary item difference compares complete diets. The processed-seed registry has no posted results. The raw-kale urgency-frequency direction remains unresolved.

In 19 healthy trained men a seven-day 3 g/day commercial cayenne capsule crossover found no between-treatment difference in fastest or mean 30-m sprint time; gastrointestinal symptom score was 6.3 times higher. Sprint speed and capsule are not everyday walking or a Parkinson trial. Existing chili FFQ study reports composite sarcopenia without a chili-specific walking contrast.

A whole Parkinson diet menu includes lovage without identifying drying or apathy by lovage exposure. Individual apathy was measured in a different dietary-pattern survey without a lovage estimate. Root extract and other botanicals called lovage do not establish direction for dried garden lovage leaves.

An extract of the dried whole celery plant altered beam and drag behavior in mice. Neither those motor proxies nor related constituents estimate dystonia after fresh culinary celery leaf in Parkinson disease.

An open-label Parkinson study reported no clear change in constipation severity or bowel frequency after a multicomponent bar containing rice bran. The effect of refined rice bran oil remains unresolved.

Oral alcoholic allspice leaf extract produced sedation and motor incoordination in animal toxicity observations. An essential-oil study also reported sedation, without a handwriting task. Ground allspice and Parkinson micrographia remain unresolved.
Morris water-maze and neurological severity outcomes after oral common chive extract in ischemic mice do not supply a clinical executive-function contrast or fresh chive ingestion effect.

The tauopathy mouse study measured REM without atonia and used peanut oil as the drug comparator vehicle. The independent Alzheimer-model study tested a drug and REM stage duration. Neither supplies dream-enactment frequency after cold-pressed oil.

Injected haloperidol nanocapsules with grapeseed oil changed vacuous chewing in rats. The movement endpoint, drug exposure and route cannot determine oral cold-pressed oil’s effect on Parkinson dystonia.

Eugenol prolonged barbiturate-induced loss of righting in rats. Post-deprivation behavior under a nanoemulsion and an allspice chemistry review do not measure natural insomnia after ground culinary allspice.

A randomized plant-rich Parkinson diet study observed no clear change in Epworth daytime sleepiness and gives no raw-carrot exposure. General-population blood carotenoid associations vary in direction, with no raw-carrot-specific result.

Injected allspice leaf extracts suppressed CNS activity in rats. The original study did not measure mood. Isolated eugenol experiments give favorable and inconclusive behavioral signals with different formulations. Ground allspice berry and Parkinson depressive severity remain unmeasured.

The Parkinson study compared a strain-specific fermented milk with acidified milk and reported only total motor scores. Its table supplies within-arm analyses with no separate hand dexterity result or between-arm motor estimate. The product is not identified as plain kefir.
A whole walnut snack had inconclusive short-term salivary-flow results. The study gives no clinical drooling estimate, cold-pressed oil exposure or Parkinson sample.

Two closely related bay-odor reports found better late visual vigilance at the lower odor load in healthy men. The earlier 11-person comparison reported p=.026 across 30 minutes and the later nine-person comparison recorded 93.8% versus 88.0% at 30 minutes. The high odor load showed no clear accuracy benefit and the samples may overlap. The exposure was inhaled; effects of eating ground bay leaf on Parkinson attention remain open.

Nigella oil rinse improved early normal-diet tolerance during mucositis, with an inconclusive day-28 comparison. Reflux registration specifies nigella-derived melanin and a GERD score. Neither isolates eating ground nigella or measures Parkinson swallowing impairment.

Self-selected Parkinson records use ground white mustard alongside broccoli seed in mixed tea; the available selected self-rated symptom records do not report a visual-hallucination-frequency comparison or isolate mustard. Spontaneous patient symptom selection and simultaneous other ingredients prevent inference.

Fresh green kiwi yielded an imprecise change in self-rated waking alertness. The controlled breakfast study gives inconclusive choice reaction-time and Stroop results after previously frozen kiwi pulp, and the separate COMPASS registry lacks results. The new kiwi meal experiment measured pig brain bioamines. These outcomes leave the direction for raw kiwi and Parkinson attention impairment unresolved.

Some allergic children had hoarseness during ground roasted hazelnut challenges. Edible oil intake, vocal loudness, and Parkinson hypophonia were not established. A separate pooled pediatric report also uses a different voice and throat outcome.

The 12-week Longvida trial found less worsening on a combined PSQI daytime dysfunction component. Few improved in either arm, and no separate sleepiness item was given. Epworth was inconclusive in another formulated trial and was unreported in the Parkinson nanomicelle study. No directional result was found for eating grated turmeric and daytime sleepiness.

2014 crossover in ten trained men, nine with exercise data, combined aqueous Russian tarragon extract or placebo with creatine in both arms; sprint peak power, mean power and total work interactions p=.92, .27 and .27. These are performance tests rather than clinical fatigue after dried culinary leaves.

Canine corn-oil diets give comparator-sensitive detection results without established refining grade. Other studies use injections, an odor-pen solvent or oil preference after induced smell loss. These exposures do not resolve the direction for ingested refined oil in Parkinson disease.

The Parkinson diet trial supplies only total motor scores. Heated oil carrying mung bean extract and Cucurbita extract studies use rodent suspension or rotarod tasks. No source isolates cold-pressed pumpkin seed oil and manual dexterity.
Among 126 adults 31.0% identified dried marjoram odor; stimulus recognition is not a treatment effect on olfactory impairment after eating marjoram.

Unspecified dill tablets and a topical preparation improved questionnaire totals in other clinical settings. The tablet source does not identify plant part or insomnia subitems. The topical baseline has a reporting conflict, and the completed extract-beverage trial has no public results. Injected mouse locomotion does not measure sleep. The dried leaf and Parkinson insomnia comparison remains open.

Exercise with inhaled Zanthoxylum limonella oil improved selected eyes-closed sway measures versus almond scent. Reach and fear-of-falling interactions were inconclusive. Related Japanese pepper improved a rodent coordination measure. Neither tests ground Sichuan pepper and Parkinson postural instability.

The essential voice tremor crossover used soybean oil of unspecified grade as placebo and measured sustained vowel amplitude modulation. It gives no isolated refined oil estimate or measure of habitual Parkinson voice volume.

Related isolated cineole or non-cardamom leaf oil experimental motor studies examine induced rodent catalepsy, with different formulations and models; opposing model outcomes cannot be reclassified as dystonia. The cardamom spice review does not supply clinical item-level dystonia data.

The Parkinson powder trial gives no posted voice-volume outcomes and diet menus do not verify individual frozen berry intake. In a separate case, hoarseness progressed after blueberry avoidance and imaging identified an anatomical cause. No study supplies a frozen-blueberry vocal-volume estimate in Parkinson disease.

Intracerebral isolated green-leaf chalcone in 6-OHDA mice improved aggregate behavior; no clinical rigidity or fresh-leaf ingestion. Separate 2024 rotenone mouse perilla seed-oil study improved pole descent, a motor-speed task, and did not measure rigidity.
